headline: Razorpay, an Indian company, has partnered with OpenAI to help brands in India plan, launch and track advertising on ChatGPT.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: an announced partnership showing OpenAI building an ad business in India, but a modest deal.
importance_line: What changed is that Indian brands now have a local partner for buying ads inside ChatGPT, which matters to advertisers and to people who will see ads in the chatbot, then to Razorpay and OpenAI, and the doubt is that no results or spending figures were given.
summary: Entrackr reports that Razorpay's marketing platform Razorpay Engage will help Indian businesses prepare product listings, launch campaigns and track results for ads on ChatGPT, with early users including Fastrack, Tata Neu and Tanishq, and with an AI agent running campaigns under human oversight from Razorpay's team. It comes as OpenAI expands ChatGPT Ads in India, and Razorpay's chief operating officer Rahul Kothari said it lets brands test the channel without building the expertise themselves.
notes: Pool source The Economic Times unreadable; Entrackr read instead.
